\caption{Welfare comparison across the closure matrix: one allocation, six
reads of it, all in percent against the reference continuation. The macro
outcomes and the indices already reported in Table~\ref{tab:results-matrix}
are dropped, so that the table isolates the welfare question. $W_C$ is the
household-consumption index of Table~\ref{tab:results-matrix}; $W_D$ the
quantity index of demand, i.e.\ the own-weights aggregate over $c+g$;
$W_{CES}$ the CES evaluation of that bundle at the \emph{baseline}
preference weights, which is what prices the composition shift the programme
imposes; $W_{CES^*}$ the same bundle evaluated at the \emph{adopted}
weights, read off the counterfactual bundle itself with $g$ subsumed into
the private part; and $W_{CES^*}^{L}$ the first-order leisure-augmented
form under the two saving conventions. The elastic-supply row is the
min--max bracket over the executed $\eta_{s,i}\in\{0.5,1,2\}$.
}
